nodes.name: Electrodeposition of metal hydroxides
nodes.procedure: Nickel foam was first washed with HCl solution (1:1) by ultrasound for 15 min to remove the surface oxide layer, then rinsed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, respectively. The copper foil and carbon cloth were washed with acetone, deionized water, and ethanol under sonication for 5 min, respectively. In a typical procedure, the potentiostatic electrodeposition was performed at -1.0 V for 10 min in a traditional three-electrode cell with the Ag/AgCl electrode as the reference electrode, platinum plate as counter electrode and a piece of NF/CC/CF (7×4 cm²) as the working electrode, respectively. 50 mL of Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.1 M) solution was used as the deposition electrolyte. The mass loading of cobalt hydroxide was around 4.3 mg cm⁻². The same procedure was used to prepare nickel hydroxide and bimetal nickel cobalt hydroxide by using the electrolyte with 0.7 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.1 M mixed solution with 0.033 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O + 0.067 M Co(NO3)2·6H2O, respectively.

nodes.name: Interfacial scaffolding PBA growth
nodes.procedure: The as-obtained Co(OH)2/CC or Co(OH)2/CF was directly immersed in 5 mL of potassium ferricyanide solution (30×10⁻³ M) for 1 h. To investigate the morphology evolution, the Co(OH)2/NF electrodes with different immersion times of 20 min, 1, 3, 6, and 11 h were performed. Then the sample was rinsed with DI water for several times. For comparison, K3Fe(CN)6 (30×10⁻³ M) solution was also replaced with K4Fe(CN)6·3H2O (30×10⁻³ M) solution and K3Co(CN)6 (30×10⁻³ M) solution to prepare CoFePBA@Co(OH)2/NF and CoCoPBA@Co(OH)2/NF, respectively. To obtain NiFePBA@Ni(OH)2 hierarchically structure, Ni(OH)2/CC, Ni(OH)2/NF were also immersed in K3Fe(CN)6 (30×10⁻³ M) solution.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM reveals PBA cubes with sizes of 50-200 nm dispersed on Co(OH)₂ nanosheets forming hierarchical cube-on-sheet structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Figure 1i) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM, Figure 1j; Figure S4, Supporting Information) images revealed that PBA cubes with sizes of 50−200 nm were dispersed on the nanosheets, further confirming the successful fabrication of the hierarchical cube-on-sheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM with SAED shows rings corresponding to (113) facet of Co(OH)₂ and (400), (222) facets of PBA confirming hybrid structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction with rings diffraction patterns (Figure 1j, inset) reveals that the outer ring is corresponding to the (113) facet of Co(OH)₂ whereas the inner rings were assigned to (400) and (222) facets of PBA, suggesting the formation of hybrid structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.50 nm for (200) facet of PBA and 0.26 nm for (102) facet of Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice spacing of 0.50 nm (Figure 1k) and 0.26 nm (Figure 1l) in high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) are assigned to the (200) facet of PBA and (102) facet of Co(OH)₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX element mapping confirms uniform distribution of K, Fe, C, N, Co, O in the cube-nanosheet structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) element mapping (Figure 1m) and linear scan (Figure S5, Supporting Information) of an individual cube-nanosheet structure further revealed the uniform distribution of elements, K, Fe, C, N, Co, O.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern indexed to α-Co(OH)₂ (JCPDS 46-0605) with additional peaks at 24.9° and 35.6° for K₂CoFe(CN)₆ (JCPDS 31-1000).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Figure 2a; Figure S6, Supporting Information) of the sample prepared by electrodeposition is well indexed to α-Co(OH)₂ (JCPDS 46-0605). With prolonging reaction time, the additional peaks... ascribed to the diffraction of K₂CoFe(CN)₆ (JCPDS 31-1000)...

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows sharp peak at 2080 cm⁻¹ attributed to stretching vibration of cyanide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with α-Co(OH)₂, the additional sharp peak of Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy centered at 2080 cm⁻¹ (Figure S6, Supporting Information) would be attributed to the stretching vibration of cyanide.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show peaks at 2086 and 2140 cm⁻¹ assigned to C≡N⁻ vibrations of cobalt ferricyanide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: On the basis of Raman spectra, the two typical peaks at 2086 and 2140 cm⁻¹ could be assigned to C≡N⁻ vibrations of cobalt ferricyanide.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Fe 2p peaks at 708.6 and 721.3 eV correspond to cyanocoordinated Fe(II); presence of K, N peaks confirms composition transformation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) peaks of Fe 2p centered at 708.6 and 721.3 eV correspond to the cyanocoordinated Fe(II) (Figure S7, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Air-calcined derivative at 450°C shows XRD peaks indexed to Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 42-1467) and Fe₃O₄ (JCPDS 26-1136) composites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD peaks (Figure S33, Supporting Information) can be well indexed to the composites of Co₃O₄ (JCPDS 42-1467) and Fe₃O₄ (JCPDS 26-1136), suggesting the thermal transformation into metal oxides.

nodes.characterization_summary: NH₃-calcined derivatives from 325-500°C show formation of CoN and FeN with decreasing nitrogen content at higher temperatures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD analysis reveals the formation of CoN and FeN (Figure S34, Supporting Information)... with elevating the reaction temperature from 325 to 500°C, the nitrogen content decreases gradually...

nodes.characterization_summary: 450°C NH₃-calcined metal nitride derivative shows lattice fringe of 0.206 nm assigned to (111) plane of cobalt nitride.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringe of 0.206 nm is assigned to the (111) plane of cobalt nitride (Figure S35, Supporting Information).
